A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VisCo research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations on MM-SafetyBench, SafeBench-Tiny, and HarmBench, together with component ablations, assistant-model comparisons, and case studies.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark and ablation results and reports additional target-model responses in its appendix case studies.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1-3.4 retain the same four context-generation strategies, auxiliary image generation, semantic assessment, iterative refinement, and attack execution. Renaming the refinement heading to include toxicity obfuscation does not introduce a new component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same three benchmarks, including 50 SafeBench-Tiny queries and the 110-example HarmBench multimodal subset. The corrected HarmBench caption and additional illustrative cases do not establish expanded dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: QR Attack, Enhanced QR, and FigStep remain in the same corresponding comparisons. Enhanced QR on regenerated images was already reported in v1 Table 4; v2 clarifies its description without adding a comparator.

E3.justification: The target models, sample counts, GPT-4o scoring procedure, best-of-five attack evaluation, three dialogue rounds, three refinement iterations, and single-attempt ablation protocol are retained. The original-versus-regenerated image explanation documents comparisons already present in v1.

E4.justification: Appendix A.3 adds scored Scenario Simulation and Image Hallucination case studies, retaining the existing Multi-Perspective Analysis and Iterative Interrogation examples. The Scenario Simulation case expands the illustration in Figure 2. Component, dialogue-length, and assistant-model ablations remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Attack-attempt counts and maximum-score aggregation remain unchanged. Neither version reports seed-based repeated experiments, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical significance tests.

E6.justification: All numerical results in Tables 1-7 and Figure 3 are unchanged. New Figures 4 and 7 add model-response examples labeled with toxicity scores of 5. Section 4.2 also correctly describes the unchanged ASR differences as percentage-point gains.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation and reasoning are retained. Equation (4) changes an inconsistent j-1 index to i-1, matching the existing prose; this is notation cleanup. No substantive assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same proposed jailbreak setting, two-stage VisCo contribution, and effectiveness claims. Changing visual-centric to vision-centric and detoxification to toxicity obfuscation does not alter their scientific scope.

C2.justification: Section 4.1 newly characterizes the four strategies as yielding comparable results and uses this to justify presenting Iterative Image Interrogation alone in the main results. The manual-template limitation and interpretations of the ablations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly identifies Enhanced QR as SD+Typo on regenerated images and maps the original and regenerated image conditions to Tables 1 and 4. These are documentation clarifications; implementation models, temperatures, attack budgets, and code access remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Miao et al. (2025), Response Attack, to the in-context-jailbreak discussion. It also replaces the Qwen Team model citation with the already-listed Yang et al. technical report. The broader research positioning is retained.

P1.justification: v2 standardizes terminology, edits grammar and citation phrasing, expands appendix cross-references, and adds author contacts and acknowledgments. It also renames Ethical Impact to Ethics Statement. The scientific narrative and section organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds two appendix case-study figures, labels and captions all four cases, enlarges retained case images, and consolidates Tables 4-7 onto one page. Captions clarify metric scales and correct Table 7's erroneous MM-SafetyBench attribution to HarmBench.

improvement.justification: v2 corrects misleading descriptions in Table 7 and the existing identity-fabrication case, clarifies baseline image conditions and percentage-point gains, and supplies examples for all four strategies. These changes improve clarity and qualitative support. The method and quantitative validation remain unchanged, so the overall improvement is limited.
